policies.title: HTTPS site does not send Strict-Transport-Security
policies.description: Checks that the Strict-Transport-Security response header is configured.
policies.rationale: Without HSTS a first plain-HTTP request can be intercepted and downgraded.
policies.absence_note: The response header is not set anywhere in the submitted file: treated as a failure (it may be set by an include or an upstream proxy, which is not visible).
policies.remediation: Add the header with max-age of at least about six months.

more_samples.negative:
SSLEngine on
Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000"

policies.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
policies.description: Checks that the X-Content-Type-Options response header is configured.
policies.rationale: Browsers may otherwise guess a dangerous content type for an upload or response.
policies.absence_note: The response header is not set anywhere in the submitted file: treated as a failure (it may be set by an include or an upstream proxy, which is not visible).
policies.remediation: Add the header with the value nosniff.

policies.title: No clickjacking protection header
policies.description: Checks that the X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors response header is configured.
policies.rationale: A page that can be framed by other sites can be used for clickjacking.
policies.absence_note: The response header is not set anywhere in the submitted file: treated as a failure (it may be set by an include or an upstream proxy, which is not visible).
policies.remediation: Set X-Frame-Options DENY/SAMEORIGIN or a CSP frame-ancestors directive.

policies.title: No Content-Security-Policy header
policies.description: Checks that the Content-Security-Policy response header is configured.
policies.rationale: A CSP limits what injected script can do.
policies.absence_note: The response header is not set anywhere in the submitted file: treated as a failure (it may be set by an include or an upstream proxy, which is not visible).
policies.remediation: Define a policy suited to the application, starting in report-only mode if needed.

policies.title: nginx enables obsolete TLS/SSL protocol versions
policies.description: Checks that ssl_protocols excludes SSLv2/3, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1.
policies.rationale: Old protocol versions have known downgrade and cipher weaknesses; major browsers dropped them.
policies.absence_note: ssl_protocols not set: the default depends on the nginx version and OpenSSL build, so the result is unknown.

policies.title: nginx enables weak cipher suites
policies.description: Checks that ssl_ciphers does not positively enable NULL, EXPORT, RC4, DES or MD5 suites (negations such as !aNULL are fine).
policies.rationale: These suites give no or trivially breakable encryption.
policies.absence_note: ssl_ciphers not set: nginx uses its built-in default list.
policies.remediation: Use a vetted modern list and keep !aNULL:!MD5 style exclusions.

policies.title: nginx reveals its version
policies.rationale: Version banners help attackers pick exploits.
policies.absence_note: Default is on (version shown in headers and error pages): treated as a failure.

policies.title: nginx directory listing is enabled
policies.description: Checks that autoindex is not on.
policies.rationale: Listings expose files nobody meant to publish.

policies.title: nginx request body size is unlimited
policies.rationale: Unlimited uploads allow disk and memory exhaustion.

policies.title: nginx workers run as root
policies.description: Checks that the user directive is not root.
policies.rationale: A bug in a worker would hand the attacker root.
policies.absence_note: Default user is nobody (or the build default) when unset.
policies.remediation: Use an unprivileged account such as www-data or nginx.

policies.title: Apache enables obsolete TLS/SSL protocol versions
policies.description: Checks that SSLProtocol disables SSLv3, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1.
policies.rationale: Old protocol versions have known weaknesses.
policies.absence_note: SSLProtocol not set: the default depends on the Apache/OpenSSL versions, so the result is unknown. The meaning of 'all' in recent versions is UNVERIFIED, so it is only accepted when the old versions are also removed.

policies.title: Apache enables weak cipher suites
policies.description: Checks that SSLCipherSuite does not positively enable NULL, EXPORT, RC4, DES or MD5 suites.
policies.rationale: These suites give no or trivially breakable encryption.
policies.absence_note: SSLCipherSuite not set: Apache uses its default list.

policies.title: Apache reveals detailed version information
policies.rationale: Detailed banners help attackers pick exploits.
policies.absence_note: Default is Full (UNVERIFIED in this research): treated as a failure.

policies.title: Apache directory listing is enabled
policies.description: Checks that no Options line enables Indexes.
policies.rationale: Listings expose files nobody meant to publish.
policies.absence_note: Default depends on the Options in effect (UNVERIFIED); not flagged when absent.

policies.title: Apache TRACE method is enabled
policies.rationale: TRACE echoes requests back and has been used in cross-site tracing attacks.
policies.absence_note: Default is on (UNVERIFIED in this research): treated as a failure.
